findings.title: Phrase text is built in growing strings that leave unwiped copies in freed memory
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Best-effort memory hygiene on the user's own offline computer; no disclosure path to another party is demonstrated.
affectedFiles: src/mhfe.rs:257 (phrase_from_entropy, used by decrypt, the rehearsal check and encrypt)
findings.reproduction: cargo run --offline --manifest-path docs/audits/AUD-005-harnesses/phrase-copies/Cargo.toml --target-dir target/aud005-phrase-copies. The probe installs a global allocator that, whenever a block is freed or moved by a reallocation, looks for the text "legal winner" in the old bytes, then calls the public mhfe::read_phrase with the public BIP39 phrase "legal winner thank year ..." typed in short upper-case forms.
findings.expected: SECURITY.md and API.md: every buffer the crate owns that holds a phrase is wiped when dropped; only working buffers inside dependencies are excepted. The crate already reserves its other phrase and password buffers at full size for exactly this reason (phrase::parse, Password::new, the terminal readers).
findings.observed: 4 freed heap blocks still held the phrase after read_phrase returned. Mnemonic::to_string writes word by word into an empty String, which grows 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 and 256 bytes; every growth frees the previous block unwiped. Only the final buffer is wiped by Zeroizing. phrase_from_entropy, which turns every recovered state into text, has the same pattern by source inspection.
findings.impact: Prefixes of an original or recovered phrase can remain in freed heap memory of the process until it is reused or the process ends, where a memory dump, swap or a later memory-disclosure bug could find them. The process is short-lived and runs offline, and the operating system discards the memory at exit, so the practical risk is small; the defect is the gap between the documented guarantee and the code.
findings.recommendedFix: Build phrase text in a Zeroizing<String> reserved at its final size (word count times nine bytes) from Mnemonic::words, as phrase::parse already does, and use it in read_phrase and phrase_from_entropy. Containers are not secret and may keep to_string.
findings.requiredVerification: The allocator probe reports 0 copies for read_phrase; a unit test shows that the buffer is never reallocated for every phrase length; the native suite and the reduced-cost container tests still pass, proving unchanged outputs.

findings.title: The weak-password warning counts a repeated dice word as several words
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Advisory heuristic only; the password is still encoded and used exactly as typed.
findings.reproduction: python3 docs/audits/AUD-005-harnesses/cli-probes.py. It runs mhfe encrypt --stdin with the public phrase "abandon ... about" and a password typed twice, under a 1 GiB address-space limit, so the tool stops with exit code 4 when it tries to reserve the 2 GiB work area, after it has judged the password and before any Argon2 work.
findings.expected: The specification asks applications to recommend at least four words chosen with dice and to warn about weak passwords; the warning text says the password is not four or more words from the EFF dice list. "abacus abacus abacus abacus" is one dice word, about 12.9 bits.
findings.observed: "abacus" gets the warning, but "abacus abacus abacus abacus" passes without it: dice_word_count counts every token that is an EFF word, including repeats.
findings.impact: A person who repeats one word, or a few words, is told nothing, although such a password is far weaker than four independent dice words. Containers and outputs are unaffected.
findings.recommendedFix: Count the different EFF words of a password made only of EFF words and warn below four, saying different words; compare case-insensitively without allocating copies of the password.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe expectation passes; unit tests cover repeats, case and non-list words; the documented warning wording matches.

findings.title: A failed memory reservation or a processor refusal recommends a memory level
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The refusal itself is correct and happens before any Argon2 work; only the added advice is wrong.
findings.reproduction: python3 docs/audits/AUD-005-harnesses/cli-probes.py (allocation part): mhfe encrypt --stdin at memory level 0 under a 1 GiB address-space limit. A processor refusal of the SSSE3 build goes through the same function (source trace; no processor without SSSE3 was available).
findings.expected: Advice should follow from the failure: a lower level helps when the computer reports too little free memory, not when a reservation the report allowed has just failed, and never for a missing processor feature.
findings.observed: "The computer could not reserve 2 GiB of memory for Argon2. The highest memory level this computer can use now is 3." Level 3 needs 6 GiB, three times what just failed. with_level_hint appends this sentence to every resource error, including ProcessorNotSupported.
findings.impact: Misleading advice in a rare failure: a user may retry, or worse, choose a higher memory level for a new container, and then need a computer with that memory for every recovery. No secret or output is affected.
findings.recommendedFix: Append the level hint only to NotEnoughMemory, the refusal that is based on the reported free memory.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe expectation passes; a unit test checks that allocation and processor refusals carry no level hint and that a memory refusal still can.

findings.title: The AUD-004 record does not name the commit of its BLD001 licence bundle
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Audit-record accuracy; no product behaviour is affected.
findings.reproduction: Read the AUD-004 remediation table at df70ca5 and compare with git log.
findings.expected: AUDIT_STANDARD: remediation tables give the fix commit and the verification commit of every finding.
findings.observed: The Markdown fix commit reads "11f2b4e999678b63b03c5e0e743c48f8658366cd (bech32 notice); this commit (generated bundle)", the JSON "the commit that adds this remediation update (generated bundle)", and the JSON remediationUpdate says "the BLD001 bundle is uncommitted". The bundle is in d4de5e8a3da0a41bc31c6b9c40a91cbdf0d36124, which also holds the record, so neither text resolves to a commit and the last statement is false at that commit.
findings.impact: A reader cannot tell from the record which commit holds the remediation it describes.
findings.recommendedFix: Name df70ca5 in both AUD-004 records, and record as a dated follow-up the verification evidence that now exists for AUD-004-FUN001 and AUD-004-BLD001.
findings.requiredVerification: Both AUD-004 records name df70ca5, agree with each other, still validate against the schema, and keep their original findings and evidence.

findings.title: API.md lists the password refusals without control characters and separators
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Documentation omission; the code refuses as the specification requires.
findings.reproduction: Compare the Password::new bullet of API.md with src/password.rs and the specification's Password encoding.
findings.expected: The specification requires a password with a control character, U+2028 or U+2029 to be rejected, never cleaned; Password::new refuses it with CONTROL_CHARACTER_IN_PASSWORD.
findings.observed: API.md says Password::new rejects an empty result, more than 1024 bytes after normalization and unassigned code points, and does not mention the control-character rule (only the error table names the code).
findings.impact: An integrator reading the API description may not expect, and may not explain, this refusal.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the rule to the Password::new bullet.
findings.requiredVerification: The bullet names every refusal of Password::new.

findings.title: README does not say that check --stdin needs a reference option
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The tool refuses clearly before reading anything.
findings.reproduction: mhfe check --stdin (no reference option); covered by cli-probes.py.
findings.expected: The script section should let a script author write a working command line; check --stdin requires --address, --fingerprint or --words (clap group, src/bin/mhfe/check.rs), as its own --help says.
findings.observed: README lists the answers for "decrypt and check" and for "check --address or check --fingerprint" but not that check --stdin without one of the three options is refused with exit code 2, nor that --words N reads only the container and the password.
findings.impact: A script written from the README fails on its first run; no wrong result is possible.
findings.recommendedFix: State the requirement and the answers for each reference option.
findings.requiredVerification: README matches the clap definition and check --help.

findings.title: client.d.ts gives readPhrase two doc comments, and tools show only the second
findings.reproduction: Read the declaration of readPhrase in web/client.d.ts.
findings.expected: One JSDoc block per declaration; TypeScript attaches only the block that immediately precedes the declaration.
findings.observed: Two consecutive /** */ blocks precede readPhrase; editors show only the otherLengths paragraph, and the sentence that the phrase comes back with every word written out is lost.
findings.impact: Integrators see an incomplete description in their editor.
findings.requiredVerification: One block precedes readPhrase; node --check of the package and verify-browser-package.mjs still pass.

informationalObservations: The browser client throws synchronously for argument and state errors (TypeError, INVALID_PIM, BUSY, PASSWORDS_DIFFER, INVALID_PASSWORD_TEXT) from methods typed as returning a Promise, and rejects only for worker errors. await handles both, a bare .catch() does not. This is long-standing, tested behaviour that the wallet tools may rely on, so it is left as a decision for the owner rather than a finding.

Carried from AUD-004: exceptions thrown by the page's onProgress or onUnverified callbacks propagate to the page's event loop and do not stop the operation; documenting this or turning it into a rejection is still open.

No Prettier configuration exists in this repository; with the mhfe_spec configuration 12 Markdown and JavaScript files differ (mostly prose wrapping and quote style). Files touched by the remediation were formatted; the rest were left as they are.

scripts/independent-suite3.py takes NFKD from Python's unicodedata, Unicode 16.0.0 on Python 3.14, and does not apply the Unicode 17.0.0 unassigned-code-point rule. This does not affect the public corpus, whose passwords use long-assigned characters, but the script is not an independent check of that rule.

Workflow hardening, not defects: vectors.yml installs cryptography==46.0.5 without a hash; the release canonical job checks out with persisted credentials (.git is excluded from the Docker context); the publish job writes SHA256SUMS over the downloaded artifacts without comparing them with the canonical job's own SHA256SUMS.
Carried from AUD-004: Linux MemAvailable is not cgroup-aware, and the macOS memory query does not release its Mach host port.

scripts/build-reproducible.sh sends the whole working tree minus .dockerignore to Docker, including untracked and ignored local files such as audit evidence and __pycache__. They do not reach the archives, which are built from named files, and CI builds from a clean checkout; a local canonical build of a modified tree is still labelled with the package version only.

When standard error is redirected but standard output is a terminal, mhfe encrypt shows the container before its check while the not-verified notice goes to the redirected stream. Prompts go there too, so this needs a deliberately unusual invocation.
Release run 36823878528 for v0.4.0 had its canonical and macOS jobs finished successfully and the full-size vector replay still running when it was read; no published release asset was compared.

remediation.evidence: New `phrase::phrase_text` writes the words into a `Zeroizing<String>` reserved at nine bytes per word; `read_phrase` and `phrase_from_entropy` use it, so recovery, the rehearsal check and encryption no longer leave growth copies. Unit test `phrase::tests::phrase_text_never_outgrows_its_buffer` (5 lengths x 64 public phrases: same text as `to_string`, capacity never grown). The probe now reports 0 copies (`remediation-sec001-probe`, log `36649a27e1b4d948ef672f2502d7749747dce53ca93da149dd61966a009f19ca`); fmt, both clippy runs and all tests with all features passed (`remediation-sec001-tests`, `ac897948acfc6ade1d7f4cb6780115fb56b69a7488e76585ffa3dc8072ac8974`); the rebuilt WebAssembly core gives the native container in both Emscripten builds (`remediation-sec001-browser`, `2ad5f6ee7a19a96fb8a3bf896398661dcd86634d577bf096f96198c13e1d1eb0`). Rechecked at 94a7e7c.

`different_dice_words` counts the different EFF words of a password made only of such words, compares tokens in place with ASCII case folding and keeps the list positions in a wiped buffer reserved at full size; the warning reads "not four or more words from the EFF dice list, all different", and README says "different". Unit test `diceware::tests::a_repeated_dice_word_counts_once`. CLI tests and clippy passed (`remediation-fun001-tests`, `de73c531abf7269ba690a177a12578f13dc028a71feebd34c9e6dbefd10da4a1`); the probe's three password expectations pass, while its UI001 expectation still failed at that commit, so the run exits 1 (`remediation-fun001-probe`, `da780d284174ece808ad60a721faea1f5072c65b708c2df2a1351f013c3549dc`). Every expectation passes at 4ace03e21ba10f17fd34196dc1368cdbd87e9e33.

`with_level_hint` adds the level sentence only to `NotEnoughMemory`. Unit test `settings::tests::only_a_free_memory_refusal_suggests_a_level` covers allocation, processor and free-memory refusals. CLI tests and clippy passed (`remediation-ui001-tests`, `1060f8bd14283e1b859576968ae45c2186aef4dba58249412ce77de7739550b9`); every probe expectation holds (`remediation-ui001-probe`, `6e674a5f5fcba348baee66580d3853529538b149b6bd461cd8ebaeb495309cc6`). The processor case is verified by the unit test, not on a processor without SSSE3.

Both AUD-004 records and the index name `df70ca5` for the BLD001 bundle. A dated follow-up in both records moves AUD-004-FUN001 and AUD-004-BLD001 to verified at `df70ca5` with the CI evidence listed under previous findings; original findings and evidence are unchanged, and the AUD-004 JSON validates against the shared schema. The historical Markdown was edited in place, not reformatted.
The `Password::new` bullet of API.md now names the control-character, U+2028/U+2029, unassigned, empty and length refusals, matching `src/password.rs`.

README's script section gives the answers of encrypt, decrypt and check separately and says that `check --stdin` needs `--address`, `--fingerprint` or `--words N`, matching the clap group and `check --help` (`remediation-docs-browser`, `af8f53075c0a4d393bbb52dd4f0c92d218a2e7705e9232300d970fd01994fc41`, prints the help line).
One doc comment precedes `readPhrase` in `web/client.d.ts`; the rebuilt package copies it unchanged and `verify-browser-package.mjs` passes (`remediation-docs-browser`).

limitations: No full-cost 2 GiB Argon2 execution, full positive or negative vector replay, or new vector generation (excluded by instruction). Recorded-key transcript checks do not recompute Argon2.
No Docker or reproducible build; canonical byte equality rests on exact-commit CI jobs, which are external evidence.
No local macOS, Windows, ARM64, Safari or mobile execution; Windows PE and the Windows binary's DLL imports were not inspected.
No independent cryptographic proof, side-channel measurement or review of dependency internals beyond their integration.

The phrase-copy probe observes the Rust heap of one process; it does not cover copies made by the operating system, the terminal or the standard library's input buffer, which SECURITY.md already names.
The processor-refusal half of AUD-005-UI001 is established by source trace, not by running on a processor without SSSE3.
No real wallet material was used; only the public phrases "abandon ... about" and "legal winner ...", the public test passwords and synthetic EFF words.
